thread:
Ana: heads up — during the canary for the new routing heuristic we saw a cluster of requests lose route affinity and get routed to v2, which triggered unexpected quota increments on those tenants. telemetry is sparse for the handshake -> eviction window. anyone else?

Mike: saw the same in eu-west-1 earlier today. short spike, ~2:12–2:15 UTC, tenants A123/B234. logs show `route_affinity=evicted` then immediate `route=default-v2`. no graceful fallback.

Sasha: this looks like the implicit eviction path we added in the sticky-cache PR (runtime branch). Could be ttl miscalc when a canary proxy returns `X-Route-Suggest` header.

Kevin: do we have a compact repro? I can turn up debug for one tenant if you hand me the token sample.

Ana: attaching clipped log snippet below. only sanitized tokens.
Ana: ```
[2026-03-19T02:12:01Z] request id=xx1 token=tok-abc route_hint=v1-sticky
[2026-03-19T02:12:02Z] route cache miss ttl_calc=0.0 evict_reason=canary-probe
[2026-03-19T02:12:02Z] route selected=default-v2 quota_charge=1
[2026-03-19T02:12:03Z] billing: tenant=A123 charge_tokens=1
```

Liz: ugh. that `ttl_calc=0.0` line is suspicious — might be a math edge with seqlen/kvcache sizing. also we recently changed header precedence where `X-Route-Suggest` overrides sticky cookie for canaries.

Sasha: right. if the canary proxy sends `X-Route-Suggest` with `force=true` we evict. But we intended force only for explicit admin probes, not normal canary traffic. maybe the probe flag is being set by our rollout agent incorrectly.

deploy-bot: Canary: rollout `routing-heuristic-v2` started (10% -> 25%) on eu-west-1 at 02:10 UTC :rocket:

Mike: related operational impact: tenants charged against v2 quota buckets for tokens generated during the eviction window. our billing pipeline attributes by `route_selected` at token-emit time — so re-routed tokens are billed to v2. tenants using pinned v1 saw unexpected usage.

Kevin: two things to triage: (1) prevent aggressive eviction during canary (short term: disable `force` on canary proxy headers), (2) fill telemetry gap: instrument `affinity_state` transitions and emit span with `evict_reason` and `selected_route` so we can plug into console alerts.

Liz: +1. also UX side — console should show a per-tenant routing change alert when their pinned route is bypassed for >30s. ops needs a quick way to refund/adjust billing for affected customers.

Ana: agreed. plan proposal: revert canary header `force` flag in proxy config (hotfix), add `affinity_transition` metric (enum: retained, evicted, reattached) in runtime (followup), and create a console banner for tenants showing any active bypass events. who can own the hotfix?

Sasha: I can push the proxy config rollback in the canary group now and roll to 0% for the suspect cohort. will also open PR for metric instrumentation.

Mike: I'll draft a short retro for billing ops and queue a billing-adjustment ticket if we see >0.5% tenant exposure.

Observability Bot: New metric `runtime.affinity_transition_count` registered (tags: region, evict_reason, tenant_class).

Liz: thanks. can we also sample the full header set for affected requests (scrubbed) and attach to the incident ticket so product can see the client-side behaviors?

Kevin: will add sampling rule for `route_affinity=evicted` events for the next 12 hours.

Ana: cool — thanks everyone. followups: Sasha (proxy rollback + metric PR), Kevin (sampling rule + traces), Mike (billing triage), Liz (console banner copy + product sync). I'll post a short status update to #incidents once rollback is confirmed. :thumbsup:
